first_impression.reaction: We're about 14 months out, so late 2027 or early 2028 is our window. The intro is calm and doesn't oversell: 'no single right time' and four actual factors. That earns a skim. But I came for 'which month' and the month-by-month section is mostly a public holiday list, not what the weather is actually like or what it does to the price.

journey.quote: The month that suits you depends on four things: how the wet and dry seasons fall, the official dates in your year, where you want to stand for the ceremony, and how far your guests are travelling.
journey.reaction: Sensible framing, and it includes our guests travelling. No 'paradise' fluff. Kept reading.

journey.quote: Nyepi falls on Monday 8 March 2027, beside the Idul Fitri holidays and collective leave, so ask your venue early how the day affects guests and suppliers.
journey.reaction: Didn't know about this at all. Exactly the insider thing that stops a nasty surprise with 80 people booking flights.

journey.quote: Once you have two or three months in mind, [talk to Wedded Concierge about your dates](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=best-time-to-get-married-in-bali&utm_content=primary) and turn them into dates a venue can hold.
journey.reaction: Bit early to be asked to talk to someone, I haven't read anything yet. Not pushy though.

journey.section: The dry months, May to September
journey.quote: **July.** No national holidays or collective leave days fall in July 2027.
journey.reaction: Fine, but that tells me nothing about July itself. Is it hot, busy, expensive? Each month reads like a calendar entry. I wanted a feel for the month.

journey.section: The dry months, May to September
journey.quote: Dry is not the same as rainless. Every outdoor ceremony in Bali still needs a covered backup, whatever the month.
journey.reaction: Honest trade-off. Better than pretending July is guaranteed sunshine.

journey.section: How to read BMKG's seasonal forecast for your year
journey.quote: A day under 5 mm is very light rain, 5 to 20 mm light, 20 to 50 mm moderate, 50 to 100 mm heavy and over 100 mm very heavy.
journey.reaction: Thorough, but am I really going to read an Indonesian climate bulletin? This is the spreadsheet homework we're trying to avoid. I'd want our planner to do this.

journey.quote: Can guests arrive or depart on 8 March, or should flights avoid that day?
journey.reaction: Good question, but it's handed back to us. Surely someone who plans Bali weddings knows the answer.

journey.section: Chapels and covered spaces, as each venue describes them
journey.quote: Notice the capacities. A chapel for 70 and a lawn for 250 suit very different guest lists, and the covered space needs to hold everyone, not only the ceremony.
journey.reaction: This is the useful bit. For 60 to 90 guests, Tresna at 70 is too tight and Purnama at 90 is right on the edge. Sending to James.

journey.quote: **Deposits.** If you move indoors or change the date, how do deposits and payments carry across, and what does the contract say in writing?
journey.reaction: Speaks straight to our hidden-costs fear. Still no hint of what the money actually is.

journey.quote: **Guest travel.** How long do transfers take from the airport and between hotels in heavy rain?
journey.reaction: That is literally my grandparents question, asked back at me with no rough answer.

journey.quote: Australians have drowned in rough seas and rip currents at popular beaches, including in Bali.
journey.reaction: True, but between drowning, volcanic ash, dengue and rabies, this list would scare Mum off Bali. I wouldn't forward this section.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you commit, so the covered plan and the weather call are settled before the deposit is paid.
journey.reaction: That's reassuring and specific. Who is accountable for the weather call is exactly what I'd ask.

journey.section: Larger guest lists travelling from Australia
journey.quote: July, September, October and November have no 2027 national holidays, which keeps supplier and travel planning simple.
journey.reaction: Helpful shortlist, but nothing about Australian school holidays or flight prices, which is what our guests will actually care about.

journey.section: Plan your month with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact, working in your time zone and quoting in AUD, and plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you.
journey.reaction: AUD and our time zone are right. But 'plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments' is the same end-to-end line everyone uses.

unanswered_questions: Does a dry-season date cost more than a wet-season one, even as a rough From AUD range?
Which months are busiest in Bali, and how far ahead do popular venues book out?
What is each month actually like day to day (heat, humidity, crowds), not just its holidays?
How do Australian school holidays line up with these months for guests with kids?
Should flights avoid 8 March 2027 on Nyepi, or can guests still land?
Roughly how long is the airport transfer to Uluwatu, Seminyak or Ubud, and in heavy rain?
Do you have a real Bali wedding (venue, month) we can look at? (deferred business detail)
Who is on the ground in Bali on the day to make the weather call: your own person or a local partner? (deferred business detail)
How does Wedded Wonderland charge: flat fee, percentage, commissions? (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact, working in your time zone and quoting in AUD, and plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you.
turn_offs_found.why: Generic end-to-end claim. Doesn't say who is accountable in Bali on the day or whether local work goes to strangers.

turn_offs_found.quote: **Weather call deadline.** By what time on the day, or the day before, do you decide between outdoor and covered, and who makes the call?
turn_offs_found.why: Vague pricing with no ranges: a whole post on choosing a month with no word on whether season changes the cost, which feeds our hidden-costs fear. The page lists questions about money but never gives a number.

would_share_with: James: the 'Chapels and covered spaces' list and the capacities line, because it tells us which wet-season backups actually fit 60 to 90 guests
My parents: the Nyepi section, because Dad books flights early and needs to avoid early March 2027. Not the health and beach safety list for Mum

cta_reaction.quote: [Talk to Wedded Concierge about your dates](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=best-time-to-get-married-in-bali&utm_content=secondary) and your shortlist becomes dates a venue can actually hold.
cta_reaction.why: Calm, no hard sell, and turning months into holdable dates is a real job we'd hand over. But no cost by season, no real Bali wedding and no transfer times yet. I'd read another post and want to see a real wedding before enquiring.

top_3_changes: Make the months feel like months: '**July.** No national holidays or collective leave days fall in July 2027.' tells me the calendar, not the experience. Add what each month is like and whether it's peak or quieter.

Answer some of the questions you hand back: 'Can guests arrive or depart on 8 March, or should flights avoid that day?' and 'How long do transfers take from the airport and between hotels in heavy rain?' need at least a rough answer.
Say whether the season changes the price (From AUD, with sign-off) and link one real Bali wedding with venue and month.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Sophie & James (planner couple): skimmed, looked for guest numbers, transfers, hidden costs and accountability
No invented brand facts; fees, on-the-ground team and real weddings listed as deferred unanswered questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored

open_questions.question: Is there a sourced answer on whether flights land at Bali airport on Nyepi, so the post can answer rather than ask?
Is any sourced seasonal pricing or peak-season information available for a From AUD note?

assumptions: Sophie & James arrived via a Google search for 'best time to get married in bali' with Bali as one early option, about 14 months out.
Business details and fee amounts are deferred and not penalised as must-fix.
Fast-mode read: read intro, takeaways, month list, venue chapels, questions and close; BMKG section and FAQ skimmed.
